name: Enfortumab vedotin
route_note: IV infusion on days 1 and 8 (with pembrolizumab) or days 1, 8 and 15 (monotherapy)

discovery.note: Fully human anti-Nectin-4 IgG1 linked by a protease-cleavable linker to monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE).

tagline: Nectin-4 ADC that, with pembrolizumab, displaced platinum chemotherapy in bladder cancer
summary: Enfortumab vedotin is an antibody–drug conjugate targeting Nectin-4, an adhesion protein highly expressed in urothelial cancer. Combined with pembrolizumab it became a first-line standard for advanced urothelial carcinoma, nearly doubling survival compared with platinum chemotherapy in EV-302.
mechanism: The antibody binds Nectin-4 on tumour cells; after internalisation, lysosomal proteases cleave the valine–citrulline linker and release MMAE.
MMAE disrupts microtubules, causing cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis, and can diffuse to neighbouring cells. Nectin-4 is also expressed in skin, which helps explain the frequent skin toxicity.
uses: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer (first line with pembrolizumab)
Urothelial cancer after a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor and platinum chemotherapy (monotherapy)

history.title: Accelerated approval
history.detail: FDA grants accelerated approval in December for previously treated urothelial cancer (EV-201).

history.title: EV-301 and full approval
history.detail: EV-301 shows a survival benefit over chemotherapy; regular approval granted.

history.title: Boxed warning
history.detail: A boxed warning for serious skin reactions, including SJS/TEN, is added.

history.title: EV-302 and first-line approval
history.detail: With pembrolizumab, it nearly doubles median overall survival versus platinum chemotherapy; FDA approves the combination in December.

history.title: Pfizer acquires Seagen
history.detail: Pfizer completes its acquisition of Seagen in December.

pk.metabolism: Antibody catabolised; MMAE metabolised by CYP3A4
pk.excretion: MMAE mainly in faeces, some in urine

serious: Stevens–Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
safety.boxed_warning: Serious and fatal skin reactions, including Stevens–Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.

facts: Pembrolizumab plus enfortumab vedotin was the first regimen to replace platinum chemotherapy as first-line standard in advanced urothelial cancer.
MMAE is the same payload used in brentuximab vedotin.
